summary: Marco Casario and Massimo provide a comprehensive analysis of current market volatility, utilizing quantitative indicators like the SOX semiconductor index and the CBOE Implied Correlation Index to assess risks. They discuss the importance of institutional liquidity levels and volume profiles for assets like the S&P 500, copper, and Bitcoin. The speakers emphasize that while current market conditions show signs of excess, a violent crash is not yet confirmed, provided key support levels hold. They advocate for strict money management and risk control over technical setups, particularly for leveraged instruments. Finally, they advise long-term investors to maintain discipline and avoid emotional decision-making driven by daily market noise.

key_points.point: Nvidia experienced a massive 33% increase following Jensen's return, showing extreme market momentum.
The SOX semiconductor index monthly returns reached peak levels comparable to the dot-com bubble and recovery bottoms.
S&P 500 and Nasdaq have experienced four consecutive positive years, signaling potential for negative years ahead.
The CBOE 1-month Implied Correlation Index (COR1M) dropped to very low levels around 3 during summer, signaling lack of protection.
Historical data shows that when the VIX exceeds 50, the S&P 500 has never closed negative one year later.
S&P 500 futures show strong institutional interest around the 6008 level, which acts as a key support.
Money management and strict risk control are more critical to survival than any technical entry setup or strategy.
Passive long-term investors should avoid daily media consumption to prevent emotional mistakes during drawdowns.

moments.claim: Market volatility drives both strong upward and downward movements across major indices.
moments.details: Recent weeks have shown high volatility, highlighted by Nvidia's massive gain following Jensen's reentry. While some believe the worst is over with the VIX falling below 20, several fragility signals remain on the table.
moments.surprise: Nvidia surged over 33% upon recent news.
moments.conclusion: Markets continue to fluctuate, and investors must remain cautious despite recent rebounds.

moments.claim: Semiconductor monthly returns show extreme excess similar to historical dot-com peaks.
moments.details: Massimo explains how monthly return histograms for the SOX semiconductor index indicate it was the second best-performing monthly surge during the uptrend, mirroring dot-com era extremes and recovery points.
moments.surprise: SOX monthly returns matched dot-com bubble highs.
moments.conclusion: Semiconductor performance has reached excessive levels that historically warrant caution.

history.story: The SOX index showed extreme monthly return spikes during the dot-com era and subsequent recoveries, culminating in recent highs.
history.parallel: Current semiconductor monthly returns mirror the extreme exuberance seen during the dot-com peak.

moments.topic: Ergodicity and anomaly counting in markets
moments.claim: Ergodicity and anomaly counting help identify market excess phases.
moments.details: Massimo explains spatial and temporal means to spot market excesses, similar to the dot-com bubble period. Poisson-based anomaly counters track abnormal volume, volatility, and momentum spikes.
moments.surprise: Poisson anomaly counters identify extreme market stress points.
moments.conclusion: Quantitative metrics confirm that market conditions reached extreme excess levels.

moments.topic: S&P 500 and Nasdaq consecutive positive years
moments.claim: S&P 500 and Nasdaq have posted four consecutive positive years, raising drawdown risks.
moments.details: Reviewing historical drawdown charts for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reveals four consecutive positive years, which is an exceptional streak. Marco and Massimo note that at least one negative year is likely in the coming 2-3 years.
moments.surprise: Four consecutive years of positive S&P 500 returns.
moments.conclusion: Investors must anticipate negative years ahead after such a prolonged positive run.

moments.claim: Low implied correlation index values signal extreme complacency and lack of downside protection.
moments.details: Examining the CBOE 1-month Implied Correlation Index (COR1M), which tracks top S&P 500 companies, shows that values dropped near 3 during the summer. Such low levels indicate that option protection costs very little because investors are not hedging.
moments.surprise: Implied correlation dropped to nearly 3 during the summer.
moments.scenario: When COR1M drops to 3-8, options become very cheap due to lack of hedging, signaling a contrarian risk warning before sharp downward moves.
moments.conclusion: Extremely low correlation index values serve as a strong contrarian risk warning.

moments.topic: Implied Correlation Index and crash risk
moments.claim: The market has ceased anticipating a crash for an extended period.
moments.details: The CBOE 1-Month Implied Correlation Index shows that the market has stopped pricing in a potential crash, which the author interprets as a sign of complacency.
moments.surprise: The market has been unprepared for shocks for a long time.
moments.conclusion: The lack of fear in the market is a key indicator to watch.

moments.claim: High VIX levels do not necessarily signal an imminent market crash.
moments.details: The author examines the VIX at 30, noting it is high relative to realized volatility but suggests the market is currently protected. He presents a scatter plot showing that when the VIX exceeds 50, the S&P 500 has historically never closed negative one year later.
moments.surprise: VIX above 50 has never led to a negative S&P 500 return one year later.
moments.conclusion: The market is currently protected, making further violent downside moves difficult.

history.story: When VIX > 50, the S&P 500 has never been negative one year later.
history.parallel: Current VIX levels, while elevated, do not imply a guaranteed crash.

moments.topic: Gold as a hedge and central bank buying
moments.claim: Gold is currently being accumulated by central banks as a strategic hedge.
moments.details: The author shows a chart of China's central bank gold buying, which has increased steadily from 260,000 to 830,000 fine troy ounces monthly. He compares gold's historical volatility to stocks, noting it goes through euphoric phases and long periods of stagnation.
moments.surprise: China's gold buying has more than tripled in a few months.
moments.conclusion: Gold is performing as expected, but investors should be aware of its cyclical nature.

history.story: Gold experiences euphoric phases followed by long periods of non-performance.
history.parallel: Current accumulation by central banks mirrors historical strategic shifts away from the dollar.

moments.claim: The 6008 level is the most critical volume node for institutional investors in 2024.
moments.details: The author points to a volume profile on the S&P 500 futures chart. He states that if 6008 holds, the market will likely continue its V-shaped recovery. If it is lost, a more significant correction starting from the 2020 highs is expected.
moments.surprise: Losing the 6008 volume node would mean institutions are no longer aggressively buying.
moments.scenario: If 6008 holds, V-shaped recovery; if lost, deeper correction.
moments.conclusion: The 6008 level is the key determinant for the market's medium-term trend.

moments.claim: Copper is showing signs of distribution because volume has shifted to the top of the range.
moments.details: The author analyzes the copper futures chart. He explains that when volume nodes move to the top of a price range, it suggests that institutional buyers are distributing their positions. This increases the probability of a downward reversal.
moments.surprise: Volume nodes at the top of a range are a bearish signal for assets.
moments.scenario: High volume at the top suggests distribution and potential price decline.
moments.conclusion: Copper is currently less attractive for long positions due to distribution signals.

moments.claim: Natural gas is showing a compression pattern that often precedes upward acceleration.
moments.details: The author highlights a compression zone in natural gas futures. He compares this to a squeezed water hose, suggesting that the pressure built during this consolidation phase will lead to a sharp upward move once the price breaks out.
moments.surprise: Price compression is a leading indicator for high-volatility breakouts.
moments.scenario: Price compresses, then accelerates upward with high pressure.
moments.conclusion: Natural gas is a strong candidate for long positions.

moments.claim: Bitcoin is approaching a historical drawdown level that makes it attractive for long-term accumulation.
moments.details: The author examines Bitcoin's volume profile and historical drawdowns. He notes that a 60% drawdown would be one of the smallest in history, suggesting strong underlying support. He plans to scale into long positions if the price reaches the 40k-50k range.
moments.surprise: Current Bitcoin drawdowns are historically small compared to previous cycles.
moments.scenario: Scale into long positions if price drops to the 40k-50k range.
moments.conclusion: Bitcoin remains a long-term buy despite short-term volatility.

history.story: Previous cycles saw drawdowns of 77% and 80%.
history.parallel: Current potential drawdown is only 60%, indicating relative strength.

moments.topic: Crypto market shocks and exchange stability
moments.claim: Binance absorbed market pressures without systemic disruption, unlike fraudulent exchanges like FTX.
moments.details: Massimo and Marco analyze past crypto drawdowns, noting that FTX's collapse was a fraud that pushed Bitcoin to temporary lows. In contrast, Binance handled significant outflows smoothly without causing market shock waves. They observe that retail interest is currently low, while institutional investors continue analyzing chain development and DeFi infrastructure.
moments.surprise: Binance repaid all user redemptions during panic without creating a broader systemic shock.
moments.conclusion: Underlying crypto liquidity remains strong even during periods of low retail engagement.

moments.claim: Bitcoin remains a software technology whose underlying adoption metrics stay constant through cycles.
moments.details: Massimo emphasizes that Bitcoin's fundamental software rules have not changed. Examining long-term volume distributions shows liquidity sits firmly at lower historical bounds, indicating retail buyers will return once market momentum flips. Investors must rebalance asset weights as holdings appreciate or decline relative to targets.
moments.surprise: Bitcoin trading volume patterns consistently show baseline liquidity support during bear market phases.
moments.conclusion: Proper asset weighting prevents overexposure when single positions surge or drop.

moments.topic: Money management and options leverage risks
moments.claim: Money management is far more important than entry setups or technical strategies.
moments.details: Marco explains that overexposing capital using leveraged instruments like options during volatility spikes (VIX hitting 40-50) is a classic mistake. If an account suffers a complete game over, trading ends permanently. Massimo agrees, urging traders not to take kamikaze risks and to maintain balanced risk limits across all asset classes.
moments.surprise: Implied volatility spikes to 40-50% can instantly wipe out over-leveraged options traders.
moments.conclusion: Risk control and position sizing dictate long-term market survival.

moments.topic: Psychology and discipline during market drawdowns
moments.claim: Passive investors must disconnect from daily news to avoid psychological stress.
moments.details: Massimo advises long-term investors experiencing drawdowns to step away from financial media, YouTube channels, and television. For short-term speculators entering stocks like NVDA, defined stop-loss thresholds are mandatory. Passive investors with 15-year horizons should let their portfolio work without checking prices every day.
moments.surprise: Checking long-term portfolios daily creates unnecessary emotional pain that leads to irrational selling.
moments.conclusion: Detachment from market noise is essential for successful passive investing.

moments.claim: Active strategies should only be executed using satellite capital separate from core holdings.
moments.details: Massimo notes that investors who want to test active trading or market timing should protect their main capital in a secure core portfolio. Only a smaller satellite portion should be allocated for active testing. Those who lack interest or time for deep research are far better off staying 100% passive.
moments.surprise: Many self-described passive investors act like short-term traders by monitoring market movements constantly.
moments.conclusion: Investors must align their actions with their chosen strategy - either fully passive or structured core-satellite.

moments.topic: Importance of market research and screening
moments.claim: Investors must conduct their own screening because many market participants are unprepared.
moments.details: The speakers note that many people in the sector improvise and lack passion. They advise listeners to be critical and avoid following those who do not share a genuine desire to learn and share knowledge.
moments.surprise: The market is full of people who are not truly passionate about investing.
moments.conclusion: Screening is essential for making informed investment decisions.

moments.claim: Consuming a wide variety of information helps investors find their own path.
moments.details: The speakers argue that listening to many different sources opens new horizons and helps individuals understand their own goals. This process allows investors to orient themselves better in the market.
moments.surprise: Listening to many sources is a tool for self-discovery in investing.
moments.conclusion: Diverse information leads to better self-orientation.

moments.claim: The market naturally filters out low-quality information and scams.
moments.details: The speakers explain that the market acts like Darwinian natural selection. Motivated investors will eventually learn to distinguish between useful information and mere deception.
moments.surprise: The market acts as a natural filter for quality.
moments.conclusion: Motivated investors will eventually find the right information.

digest_it: Marco Casario e Massimo analizzano la volatilità e gli indicatori quantitativi di eccesso sui mercati azionari, confrontando la situazione attuale con i cicli storici. Spiegano come utilizzare medie mobili, profili di volume e tassi di correlazione per valutare i rischi ed evitare di farsi sorprendere dai ribassi. Sottolineano l'importanza cruciale del money management e della disciplina psicologica per gli investitori, invitando a ignorare il rumore mediatico quotidiano e a mantenere un approccio basato su una solida gestione del rischio.
title: Quando i Mercati SCENDONO: prima di Comprare guarda questi Segnali
author: Marco Casario EXTRA
